# Recommender Systems from Zero

> A free, hand-checkable, from-zero handbook on recommender systems: a vertical path from linear algebra and calculus through losses, neural networks and the Transformer, to graph- and LLM-based collaborative filtering (LightGCN, contrastive SSL, the spectral view, RLMRec), plus how to train and serve a recommender. Every worked example is reproducible by hand.

Authors: Duong Tan Nghia (HUST · Minastik) and Tran Manh Hoang (HUST). Open access, CC BY 4.0. This is the web reading edition of Version 2.0 (31 October 2026) hosted by Minastik; the citable record (PDF + DOI) is on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20952962). Mathematics is rendered with MathJax and every chapter carries small, hand-verifiable numerical examples.

- [Preface — start here](https://minastik.com/recsys/): how to read the book, what it assumes, the reading order.

## Mathematical foundations
- [Linear Algebra for Machine Learning](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/linalg-foundations.html): Vectors, matrices, dot products and norms — the linear algebra recommenders are built on.
- [Calculus for Machine Learning](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/calculus-foundations.html): Derivatives, gradients and the chain rule behind gradient descent.
- [Probability & Statistics for Machine Learning](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/math-foundations.html): Probability, expectation, Bayes' rule, entropy and significance testing from scratch.

## Machine-learning fundamentals
- [Loss Functions & Regularizers](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/losses-and-regularizers.html): Squared-error, cross-entropy, BPR and softmax losses and the regularizers used to train recommenders.
- [Neural Networks & Back-propagation](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/neural-networks.html): From a single neuron to multilayer networks, backpropagation and embeddings.
- [Representation Learning & the Transformer](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/nlp-and-transformers.html): Tokenization, attention and the Transformer architecture.

## Recommender-system foundations
- [Traditional Recommender Systems](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/traditional-recsys.html): Content-based, neighborhood and matrix-factorization collaborative filtering.
- [Evaluation Metrics](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/recsys-metrics.html): How recommendation quality is measured and compared — Recall@K, NDCG, significance tests, bias and fairness.

## Sequence-based recommenders
- [Sequential & Session-Based Recommendation](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/sequential-recsys.html): Session- and sequence-based next-item recommendation.

## Graph-based recommenders
- [From Graphs to LightGCN](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/gcn-to-lightgcn.html): Graph convolution networks simplified to LightGCN for collaborative filtering.
- [Self-Supervised & Contrastive Learning](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/gcl-and-ssl-recsys.html): Graph contrastive learning and self-supervised signals for recommendation.
- [The Spectral / Graph-Filter View](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/spectral-graph-filter-cf.html): The spectral / graph-signal-processing view of collaborative filtering.

## The LLM era
- [Large Language Models and Recommendation: the Landscape](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/llm-recsys-survey.html): Four roles a large language model can play in a recommender, and what each costs and gains.

## Building a recommender
- [Training and Serving a Recommender](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/training-and-serving.html): Negative sampling, a training step, two-tower retrieval with an ANN index, and the retrieve-then-rank funnel.

## Frontiers
- [Click-Through Rate Prediction & Feature Interactions](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/deep-ctr.html): Deep models for click-through-rate prediction.
- [Bandits & Online Recommendation](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/bandits.html): Multi-armed and contextual bandits for online recommendation.

## Appendices
- [Appendix A — Implementation Choices: A Practitioner’s Field Guide](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/implementation-choices.html): Which embedding models, vector indexes, rerankers, frameworks and tools to use, and how to check dated claims.
- [Appendix B — Datasets & Benchmarks](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/datasets-and-benchmarks.html): Public datasets, splits, k-core filtering and benchmark pitfalls.
- [Appendix C — Generating Features with Large Language Models](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/llm-feature-generation.html): Using LLMs to generate user and item features.
- [Appendix D — Reinforcement Learning for Recommendation](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/rl-recsys.html): Reinforcement-learning approaches to recommendation.
- [Appendix E — Federated & Privacy-Preserving Recommendation](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/federated-recsys.html): Federated and privacy-preserving recommendation.

## Reference matter
- [Glossary](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/glossary.html): Every key term used in the book, defined alphabetically in one place.
- [List of Symbols](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/notation.html): The symbols that recur across the book, grouped by where each is introduced.
- [Appendix F — Solutions to Exercises](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/solutions.html): Worked solutions to the book's exercises.
- [Acknowledgements](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/acknowledgements.html): The people who made the book possible.
- [About the Authors](https://minastik.com/recsys/chapters/about-the-authors.html): The two authors, lecturers at the Hanoi University of Science and Technology.
